  • Priority of NMIMS and selection expectations:
  • The candidate discusses their prioritization of NMIMS among other B-schools and expresses their views on the likelihood of selection.
  • Funny incident:
  • The candidate shares a light-hearted and amusing personal experience.

Interview 2 (Engineer with work experience at Deloitte):

  • Why engineers are opting for MBA:
  • The candidate explains the trend of engineers pursuing MBA and potentially touches upon their own motivations.
  • Deloitte job satisfaction and reluctance for a change:

  • Proud moments at Deloitte and interview preparation:

  • Choice of specialization and lessons from extracurricular activities:

Interview 3 (Work experience at Infosys):

Based on common themes in Group Discussion and Personal Interview (GDPI) experiences for NMIMS and similar institutions, here are 20 frequently asked questions:
Introduce yourself.
Why do you want to pursue an MBA?
Why are you interested in NMIMS specifically?
What are your short-term and long-term career goals?
Describe your strengths and weaknesses.
Can you discuss a significant achievement in your life?
Have you faced any failures or challenges? How did you handle them?
What are your hobbies and interests?
Who is your role model, and why?
Why did you choose your undergraduate major?
How does your academic background relate to your MBA aspirations?
Do you have any work experience? If so, what did you learn from it?
Why do you want to specialize in [Marketing/Finance/Operations/etc.]?
What are your expectations from this MBA program?
How do you stay updated on current affairs and business news?
Can you discuss a recent news event that caught your attention?
What differentiates a good manager from a good leader?
How do you handle criticism or feedback?
Where else have you applied, and what other calls have you received?
Do you have any questions for us?
NMIMS MBA Admissions Overview:
NMIMS is a prestigious university offering MBA programs across multiple campuses, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Indore, Hyderabad, and Navi Mumbai. It consistently ranks among the top 25 management institutes in India, according to NIRF rankings. Apart from the General MBA program, NMIMS offers specializations in Human Resources, Pharmaceuticals Management, Digital Transformation, Business Analytics, Family Business Management, and more. Admissions are based on the NMAT entrance test scores, with final selection considering academic records, achievements, work experience, and performance in Written Ability Test (WAT) and Personal Interview (PI).
Selection Process for MBA Admissions:
Shortlisting: Based on NMAT scores.
Written Ability Test (WAT):
Paragraph-based topics with opinions to be expressed in 200-300 words.
Examples of WAT topics provided.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences:
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview Interview 1 (B.A. in Economics, Fresher):
Where are you from?
This is a common icebreaker question to learn about the candidate's background and place of origin.
Can you tell three differences between Mumbai and Delhi?
The interviewer is assessing the candidate's awareness of different cities and their ability to compare and contrast aspects.
What are your views on the current Indian economy?
This question aims to evaluate the candidate's understanding of economic issues and their ability to provide informed opinions.
What steps do you think the government should take to improve the condition of the economy?
Here, the interviewer is testing the candidate's critical thinking and policy suggestions related to economic improvement.
Why do you want to do an MBA?
The candidate is expected to articulate their motivations and goals for pursuing an MBA, providing insights into their career aspirations.
What are your views on the ‘Make in India’ campaign in India?
This question assesses the candidate's awareness of government initiatives and their opinions on strategies to promote indigenous manufacturing.
Name a leader you look up to.
The candidate is prompted to identify and discuss a leader they admire, allowing the interviewer to gauge the candidate's values and influences.
Why did you leave Mumbai and move to Delhi?
The interviewer seeks to understand the reasons behind the candidate's relocation, exploring personal and professional aspects.
What do you mean by sustainability?
This question assesses the candidate's understanding of sustainability concepts, which is relevant in various contexts, including business and the environment.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview  (B.Com, Fresher):
So, you are in your final semester at college?
The interviewer initiates the conversation with a straightforward question about the candidate's current academic status.
What elective did you choose? Why an MBA?
The candidate is asked about their academic choices and the rationale behind pursuing an MBA, exploring their educational and career motivations.
What is organizational behavior? If you're not sure then why did you want to take it?
This question evaluates the candidate's understanding of organizational behavior, with a follow-up query about their decision to study the subject.
What are the big four companies in audit?
The candidate is expected to name and possibly discuss the significant audit firms, demonstrating their knowledge of the industry.
What is the difference between preference and equity shares?
This question assesses the candidate's familiarity with financial concepts, specifically the distinctions between different types of shares.
Why do you want to do an MBA as a fresher?
The candidate is prompted to provide reasons for pursuing an MBA without prior work experience, highlighting their motivations and goals.
Why didn’t you take that job offer?
The interviewer explores the candidate's decision-making process regarding a job offer, seeking insights into their career choices.
What does an investment banker do? What are the factors they consider when advising their clients?
These questions assess the candidate's understanding of investment banking functions and the factors influencing financial advisory decisions.
What is the current interest rate for savings deposits?
The candidate is expected to demonstrate awareness of current financial trends, specifically related to interest rates on savings.
What do you have to say about the recent bank scams? Are you sure it's PMC and not PNB?
The interviewer delves into the candidate's awareness of recent banking controversies, testing their knowledge and attention to detail.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview (B.Tech in Electronics, Fresher):
So, where are you from?
Similar to the first interview, this serves as an introductory question to learn about the candidate's background.
Tell me something about Pune?
The candidate is prompted to share information about a city, assessing their awareness of localities.
Which branch did you do your engineering in? What is the difference between analog and digital electronics?
The interviewer explores the candidate's technical background, focusing on the branch of engineering and core concepts.
Which specialization are you interested in, in MBA?
The candidate is asked about their MBA specialization preferences, indicating their initial thoughts on future academic and career paths.
So you are coming with an open mind? Which subjects do you think will help you in deciding?
The interviewer explores the candidate's approach to MBA, emphasizing an open-minded perspective and discussing relevant academic interests.
What all MBA related books did you read to help you in your MBA?
The candidate is asked about their preparatory efforts, including reading materials related to MBA studies.
But why an MBA now? Why not go for a job?
The interviewer queries the candidate's decision to pursue an MBA immediately after graduation, exploring their motivations and career considerations.
Why are your marks in 12th so low? Then how much did you score in graduation?
The candidate is asked to explain academic performance, addressing any concerns about past scores and providing context.
What other calls do you have?
The interviewer seeks information about the candidate's application status and potential options, understanding their choices among different institutions.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview (B.Tech in Mechanical, 2 years of work experience):
Why did you go all the way from Bhubaneswar to Burla to do engineering?
The interviewer explores the candidate's decision-making process regarding their choice of college and location.
You took a drop of a year between 12th and Engineering? And yet you landed up in VSSUT and no NIT or IIT?
The candidate is asked to explain the gap year and elaborate on their choice of engineering institution.
Then you got placed in Hindalco which you quit after two years to work with an NGO as a management trainee? Explain about your work at Hindalco. How did you go about it?
The interviewer delves into the candidate's professional journey, exploring transitions between industries and roles.
What are your hobbies?
The candidate is prompted to discuss their hobbies, providing insights into their interests and activities outside of work.
Okay then tell me about two current affairs that you think matter. Elaborate about each topic at length. Why didn't Kyoto protocol work and why this could work?
The interviewer assesses the candidate's awareness of current affairs and their ability to analyze and discuss global issues.
What is the difference between Quality controls and Quality Assurance? What is TQM? What is six sigma?
These questions evaluate the candidate's knowledge of quality management concepts and methodologies.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview  (B.Tech in ECE, Work Experience in Tech Mahindra, freelance writer):
Tell me about yourself. What did you do in Tech Mahindra? So did you do coding? Did you get through campus recruitment?
The candidate is asked to provide an overview of their background, work experience, and the nature of their work in Tech Mahindra.
Why did you leave your job?
The interviewer explores the reasons behind the candidate's decision to leave their job, understanding motivations for career changes.
Do you read? What was the last book you read? Give me a critical analysis of Animal Farm. Not a summary but a critical analysis.
The candidate is prompted to discuss their reading habits and provide a critical analysis of a specific literary work.
So will you discontinue MBA if anything happens again? How was your IT job related to content writing? Why did you do it? Such drastically different domains? What tool?
These questions explore the candidate's commitment to pursuing an MBA, their ability to handle challenges, and the connection between their IT job and content writing.
Do you want to continue this as a major career? Ok, now that you are a creative individual tell me why we should select you. Give me an out of box answer.
The interviewer seeks insights into the candidate's future career aspirations and requests a creative response to justify their selection.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview (B.Tech, 18 months of work experience in Big4):
What is an LLP? You have 18 months of work experience; tell me something interesting about your work. (some cross-questioning)
The candidate is tested on their knowledge of business structures (LLP) and is asked to share interesting aspects of their work experience.
What would be your specialization? What do you know about marketing? What are the 7 Ps of marketing? Why do you think online food ordering apps like Zomato are booming? in marketing terms?
These questions assess the candidate's specialization preferences, marketing knowledge, and understanding of industry trends.
What are the recent trends in marketing? What do we call such type of marketing? Your school was in the news for wrong reasons. If you were the marketing head, what would be your response to it? Explain me in marketing terms, what specific marketing techniques would you use? Are you aware of any product that might have done this type of marketing recently?
The interviewer evaluates the candidate's awareness of marketing trends, crisis management, and their ability to apply marketing concepts to real-world situations.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview 4 (B.Tech in CSE, Fresher):
What is so good about the afternoon? What are the values and qualities that you have? Why are you a part of the E-cell, did no other club select you? What did you contribute as head of the E-cell?
The candidate is asked about personal qualities, involvement in extracurricular activities, and contributions as a leader in the E-cell.
Who is your favorite entrepreneur and why? Being a CS student, you have studied mobile applications, networks and all, so tell me the difference between 2G and 3G. What is the difference between AI and ML?
These questions explore the candidate's interests, knowledge of technology, and understanding of key concepts related to their field of study.
What specialization do you want to take? Tell me three strengths that you bring to the table, which would be of value at NMIMS. Tell me a little about your family background. Tell me about a problem that the company in which your father is working is facing. Do you have any siblings?
The candidate is prompted to discuss their specialization preferences, strengths, family background, and provide insights into their understanding of industry challenges.
NMIMS MBA Interview Experiences | Interview (Startup Owner)
Tell me about yourself:
The candidate provides an overview of their background, including personal and professional aspects.
What are your hobbies:
The candidate shares their personal interests and activities outside of their startup.
Tell us about your startup:
The candidate discusses the nature, goals, and achievements of their startup.
What are your long-term goals:
The candidate outlines their aspirations and plans for the future.
CAT percentile and travel choice:
The candidate addresses questions related to their CAT percentile and explains the choice of flight over train travel.
Five reasons for not selecting you:
The candidate is challenged to present potential weaknesses or areas where they might not be the ideal choice.
Priority of NMIMS and selection expectations:
The candidate discusses their prioritization of NMIMS among other B-schools and expresses their views on the likelihood of selection.
Funny incident:
The candidate shares a light-hearted and amusing personal experience.
Interview 2 (Engineer with work experience at Deloitte):
Why engineers are opting for MBA:
The candidate explains the trend of engineers pursuing MBA and potentially touches upon their own motivations.
Deloitte job satisfaction and reluctance for a change:
Questions probe the candidate's satisfaction at Deloitte and explore why they aren't considering a job change.
Proud moments at Deloitte and interview preparation:
The candidate reflects on accomplishments at Deloitte and discusses their interview preparation.
Favorite food outlets in Bangalore and city-related questions:
The candidate talks about their preferences for food outlets and answers questions about Bangalore's lakes, foam, and the city's nickname.
Choice of specialization and lessons from extracurricular activities:
The candidate discusses their preferred MBA specialization and reflects on lessons learned from extracurricular activities during graduation.
Interview 3 (Work experience at Infosys):
Infosys-related questions:
The candidate is quizzed about Infosys, including the leadership, revenue, and the Sikka-Murthy feud.
Job responsibilities at Infosys and specialization choice:
The candidate provides insights into their responsibilities at Infosys and discusses their preferred MBA specialization.
Why NMIMS and SCM for social issues:
The candidate explains their choice of NMIMS and discusses how Supply Chain Management (SCM) can be applied to address social issues.
Interview 4 (Fresher):
Feelings about being the last candidate and life story in a minute:
The candidate shares their sentiments about being the last candidate and succinctly narrates their life story.
Choosing HR with a tech background and startup-related questions:
The candidate explains the decision to choose HR despite having a tech background and responds to questions about starting their own startup.
Three qualities of HR personnel and reasons for HR course suitability:
The candidate lists three qualities relevant to HR roles and provides three reasons why they are suitable for an HR course.

IIM Shillong PGP Admissions 2022: Overview and Experiences
Introduction:
IIM Shillong, the 7th IIM established in India, is renowned for instilling ethical leadership and responsible managerial skills. The institute offers a two-year full-time PGP in management with a focus on sustainability and innovative business approaches. Selection is based on CAT scores, academic performance, and interview evaluations.
Selection Process:
Shortlisting:
Based on CAT score and overall profile.
Personal Interview (PI):
Extensive evaluation by a panel of two members.
Varied focus on academic knowledge, general awareness, and work profile.
Extempore Topics:
Candidates were assigned extempore topics during the interview, allowing one minute to think and one minute to speak. Topics covered ongoing/trending issues and were sometimes tailored to the candidate's educational background:
Profit as a dirty word in the Indian dictionary
Private vs. Public Education: Future of India
Responsible consumption or Responsible Production?
Impact of E-commerce discounts on customers
Legality of business lobbying in India
Allocation of investments in Defence vs. Education
Sustainability vs. Livelihood
Interview Experiences (Selected Candidates):
Interview 1:
Background: B.Tech (Production Engineering), Working at Citicorp
Questions:
Impact of E-commerce discounts on customer behavior.
Achieving profitability in loss-making companies.
Lean Manufacturing and its application at Citicorp.
Views on Russia-Ukraine conflict and India's stance.
Leisure activities and opinions on current events.
Interview 2:
Background: B.Com, Fresher, CAT Percentile: 98.5
Questions:
Socio-demographic factors characterizing a middle-class family.
Digital life's impact on India, merits, and demerits.
Handling a notice under income tax law.
Research design vs. research methodology.
Knowledge about Philip Kotler and marketing theories.
Special aspects of Shillong.
Interview 3:
Background: B.Tech (Chemical Engineering), 15 months Work Ex at TCS
Questions:
Overview of treatment plants and their significance.
Role of a chemical engineer in helping Ukraine.
Slope of a linear equation.
Future outlook for India and ways to counter climate change.
Growth potential in Indian sectors, functioning of insurance companies.
Interview 4:
Background: Dual degree in Metallurgy/Financial engineering, Fresher, CAT Percentile: 99.97
Questions:
Getting the poor to support sustainability.
Linking metallurgy and finance.
Significance of the iron-carbon diagram.
Insights on global market volatility, crude oil prices, and FIIs.
Recent news events and predictions about crude oil prices.
Conclusion:
The interview experiences reflected a comprehensive evaluation of candidates, covering academic, professional, and current affairs aspects. Candidates faced diverse questions, requiring critical thinking and a broad understanding of topics. Overall, the selection process aimed at identifying well-rounded individuals with the potential for responsible leadership.

title: IIM Lucknow Top 30 Interview Questions | GDPI experiences
body_html:
Here are 30 interview questions taken from IIM Lucknow GDPI experiences:

General/Personal Background

  1. Calls received and justification for low percentile.
  2. Why pursue IT after Engineering / Bcom / BMS?
  3. Why do you want to join IIM Lucknow over IIM Calcutta?
  4. What makes someone a huge failure in life?
  5. Why are you transitioning from architecture to an MBA?

Work Experience

  1. Questions related to work at Amazon, inventory management, and forecasting.
  2. Detailed discussion about your work at XXXXX, especially in the YYYYY sector.
  3. What is your approach to calculating the cost of a project?
  4. How do you calculate the Bill of Quantities for a construction project?
  5. Can you explain the challenges faced during your UPSC journey and why you shifted focus to MBA?

Technical Knowledge

  1. Prove why x^0 = 1.
  2. What is the difference between binomial distribution and Poisson distribution?
  3. Explain inheritance and polymorphism.
  4. How does Newton-Raphson's method work?
  5. What are Type I and Type II errors? Provide examples.

Current Affairs & General Awareness

  1. Discuss Punjab’s economic decline and the brain drain issue.
  2. What do you know about the Khalistan movement?
  3. Share your opinion on the Adani controversy and its impact on the economy.
  4. What are your views on farm laws in India?
  5. Explain the historical and geographical significance of Muzaffarpur.

Ethical/Situational Questions

  1. If asked to sell poison to increase shareholder value, would you do it? Why or why not?
  2. How would you handle a conflict between Vaastu principles and architectural design?
  3. Imagine you are tasked with designing a sustainable housing project. What are your priorities?
  4. Discuss whether media freedom should be unrestricted or censored.
  5. How would you react to an ethical failure in your leadership?

Academic/Subject-Specific

  1. What is the significance of the GDP in understanding the economy?
  2. Explain the third law of thermodynamics and its implications.
  3. Draw and explain the graph of y=x+4
  4. What are the principles of Vaastu, and how can they be balanced with modern architecture?
  5. What are the applications of the simplex method in chemical engineering?

These questions are directly drawn from the IIM Lucknow GDPI experiences and reflect the specific themes and experiences described below.

IIM Lucknow Personal Interview Experiences:

  1. Interview 1:
  • Date: 28th Jan
  • Location: Bangalore
  • WAT Topic: Media Freedom - Should it be given or censored?
  • Panel: 2 mid-40s male
  • Questions:
    • Calls received and justification for low percentile.
    • Discussion on business case studies where IT revolutionized processes.
    • Questions related to work at Amazon, inventory management, and forecasting.
    • Competitors of Amazon and financial questions.
  • Overall, a good interview with no intense grilling.
  1. Interview 2:
  • Profile: 10/9/8, CAT: 99.42%
  • Questions:
    • Introduction followed by technical queries about cricket.
    • Favorite subjects, especially related to IT.
    • In-depth questions on database management, inheritance, polymorphism.
    • Discussion on finance, cash flows, and Indian political figures.
    • Spontaneous extempore on cricket.
  • The interviewers were chill and the conversation was well-paced.
  1. Interview 3:
  • Date: 21 Feb 2023
  • Location: IIML Noida Campus
  • Profile: GEM with 37 months work experience in CRM
  • Questions:
    • About the candidate's background, work, and why pursue IT after Civil Engineering.
    • Questions about Punjab's economic decline, brain drain, Khalistan movement.
    • Discussion on Adani, economy, and other call preferences.
  • A conversational interview, around 10-12 minutes.
  1. Interview 4:
  • Profile: Economic Honours
  • Language: Hindi
  • Questions:
    • Mythological questions about Draupadi, Kanpur, and a Kanpuriya joke.
    • Dance-related questions, difference between dance forms, and mudras.
    • Economics-related questions, GDP, and work experience.
    • Random questions about the number of red ties in the WAT and chair pointing.
  • A quirky and random interview experience.
  1. Interview 5:
  • Date: 22nd Feb 2023
  • Background: Economic Honours
  • Questions:
    • Random questions about mythology, Kanpur, dancing, economics, and current affairs.
    • Questions about GDP, ABM preference, personal experience ethics, and WAT observation.
    • Random questions about the number of red ties and chair pointing.
  • An interview with a mix of quirky and conventional questions.

These experiences provide insights into the varied nature of IIM Lucknow interviews, ranging from technical questions to random and unexpected ones.

A Statement of Purpose (SOP) is a concise and structured essay typically required during academic or job applications. It serves as a personal introduction and a persuasive document explaining your motivations, aspirations, qualifications, and goals related to the specific program or position you're applying for. The aim is to convince the selection committee or employer that you are a suitable candidate by showcasing your unique qualities, experiences, and passion.

In about 300 words, an SOP outlines:

  1. Introduction: Briefly introduce yourself, your educational background, and any relevant experiences that have shaped your interests in the field.
  2. Motivations and Goals: Explain why you're interested in pursuing the particular program or role. Highlight your motivations, aspirations, and how this opportunity aligns with your career objectives.
  3. Relevant Experiences: Share specific instances or experiences that showcase your skills, knowledge, and passion for the field. This could include academic projects, internships, research, or work experiences.
  4. Fit with the Program/Position: Demonstrate your understanding of the program/position by discussing how its curriculum, faculty, resources, or company values align with your goals. Explain how you'll contribute to the community or organization.
  5. Conclusion: Summarize your key points, reiterate your enthusiasm for the opportunity, and express gratitude for considering your application.

Crafting an effective SOP involves precision in language, a clear structure, and authenticity. It's a chance to tell your story and present yourself as a standout candidate. Tailoring each SOP to the specific institution or job is crucial to demonstrate your genuine interest and suitability for the role or program.

title: Killer Hobbies in Interviews
body_html:
Hobbies are personal passions that offer a break from work's demands. They encompass diverse interests, from painting and cooking to hiking and gaming. Engaging in hobbies fosters creativity, cultivates patience, and hones problem-solving skills. Whether it's through team sports, solitary reading, or crafting, hobbies provide avenues for personal growth and self-expression. They offer relaxation, rejuvenation, and a chance to explore new horizons. Additionally, hobbies often build communities, connecting individuals who share similar interests. Embracing hobbies enriches life beyond professional pursuits, contributing to a well-rounded and fulfilled existence, nurturing mental well-being, and often offering unexpected avenues for learning and skill development.

Killer Hobbies in Interviews

  • Reading Fiction Novels and Non Fiction
  • Artistic activities such as painting or graphic design
  • NGO / Community service
  • Cooking or baking
  • Fitness Enthusiast! Exercising and healthcare
  • Indoor / Outdoor activities
  • Playing an instrument
  • Team or individual sports
  • Travel
  • Woodworking or other projects
  • Writing or blogging or Vlogging
  • Dancing & Dancing
  • Watching Documentary movies
  • Listening Podcasts

Questions on Hobbies in Interviews

Employers often ask about hobbies during interviews to get a sense of your personality, interests, and how well you might fit within the company culture. Here are some common interview questions related to hobbies:

  1. What do you like to do in your free time?
  2. Can you tell me about any hobbies or interests that you're passionate about?
  3. How do your hobbies contribute to your professional life?
  4. Do you have any hobbies that have taught you valuable skills?
  5. Have you ever taken a hobby and turned it into a project or initiative?
  6. Can you share a hobby or interest that you feel represents who you are?
  7. How do your hobbies demonstrate your ability to work in a team or independently?
  8. Have your hobbies ever helped you overcome a challenge or obstacle?
  9. Do your hobbies align with the skills or values needed for this position?
  10. How do you maintain a balance between your hobbies and professional responsibilities?

When answering these questions, try to relate your hobbies back to the skills, values, or experiences that could be relevant to the job you're applying for. This can help the interviewer see how your personal interests might align with the company's needs.

title: Killer Strengths for Interviews
body_html:
Certainly! Here are some of the most common strengths that are often highlighted in interviews:

  1. Communication Skills: The ability to convey ideas clearly, listen actively, and articulate thoughts effectively.
  2. Problem-solving: Demonstrating analytical skills and the ability to approach challenges with creative and effective solutions.
  3. Adaptability/Flexibility: Being open to change, quick to learn new concepts, and able to work effectively in different situations.
  4. Teamwork/Collaboration: Working well with others, contributing ideas, and supporting team goals to achieve success collectively.
  5. Leadership: Taking initiative, guiding others, making decisions, and inspiring/motivating a team toward a common goal.
  6. Time Management/Organizational Skills: Prioritizing tasks, meeting deadlines, and efficiently managing workload and resources.
  7. Attention to Detail: Being thorough, meticulous, and ensuring accuracy in work to avoid errors.
  8. Resilience/Perseverance: Having the ability to bounce back from setbacks, remain determined in the face of challenges, and maintain a positive attitude.
  9. Creativity/Innovation: Thinking outside the box, bringing fresh perspectives, and proposing novel solutions or ideas.
  10. Emotional Intelligence: Understanding and managing emotions, empathizing with others, and fostering positive relationships.

When discussing strengths in an interview, it's beneficial to not just state the strength but also provide specific examples or instances where you've demonstrated these strengths in action. This helps validate your claim and gives the interviewer a clear understanding of how you apply these strengths in a work context.

title: Killer Introduction | Introduce yourself | Tell something about yourself | Interview Skills
body_html:
Introducing yourself in an interview is an essential opportunity to make a strong first impression. Here's a comprehensive guide on how to introduce yourself effectively in an interview:

Opening Statement:

"Hello, my name is [Your Name], and I am thrilled to be here today interviewing for [specific position or role]. I bring [X years] of experience in [relevant industry/field], and I am excited to discuss how my skills and expertise align with the needs of this role at [Company Name]."

Professional Background:

"I have a solid background in [specific skills or areas relevant to the job], honed through my experiences at [previous company/ies] where I held roles such as [mention previous positions]. In these roles, I was responsible for [briefly describe key responsibilities or achievements]. These experiences have equipped me with a deep understanding of [mention relevant industry trends or challenges]."

Key Strengths:

"One of my key strengths is my ability to [highlight one or two skills that are highly relevant to the position]. For instance, I excel in [mention a specific skill such as problem-solving, leadership, communication, etc.]. title: Idol Ideal in Life! Role Model!!
body_html:
Who is your Idol in life!
 Though business and entrepreneurship in India isn't new, Indian companies and businesses has come a long way. There are numerous Indians who became famous due their businesses and their companies are listed on the Fortune 500 and a huge number of them have become billionaires.

Budding and fledgling MBAs businessmen and women looking for inspiration would do well to study the achievements of India's greatest businessmen and make them their Idol / Ideal. Some on the list are especially inspiring because they managed to make their fortune during British rule when the environment was not conducive for business and particularly for Indian business and some of them made fortune in the 21st century. The businessmen who succeeded in that environment went the extra mile to succeed. This list will give you a broad outline of the amazing journey some of these tycoons took. Let's jump into the list celebrate the achievements of some of these greats.

15 Famous business personalities in India Male

1. Dhirubhai Ambani

For a very long period, Dhirubhai Ambani was regarded as one of India’s most prominent corporate figures. He was raised by a local schoolteacher and is remembered by friends and family as being very ambitious and risk-taking. Ambani relocated to Yemen when he was 16 years old, where he marketed oil-related goods. Mukesh and Anil, his sons, were born in Yemen around this time. Ambani established Reliance Commercial Corporation in 1966, and in 1973 it changed its name to Reliance Industries. Reliance Industries had risen to become one of the largest businesses in India by the time of his passing in 2002.

2. J R D Tata

Jehangir Ratanji Dadabhoy Tata was one of the most significant Indian businesspeople of the 20th century, born into a wealthy Parsi home to renowned businessman Ratanji Dadabhoy Tata and a French mother, Suzanne Briere. He spent the majority of his formative years in France and England, finally giving up his French nationality in 1929 to become an Indian citizen. Being the country’s first licenced pilot, J R D Tata is frequently referred to be the founder of Indian air travel. He established Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in 1968, Voltas in 1954, Tata Motors in 1945, Tata Salt in 1983, and Titan Industries in 1987. In 1992, he received the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian distinction.

3. Kunal Bahl

Kunal Bahl, an Indian investor and entrepreneur who was born and raised in Delhi, co-founded the Indian online retailer Snapdeal with a colleague from school, Rohit Bansal. The Wharton School awarded a management degree to Bahl, while IIT Delhi awarded a BTech to Bansal. In 2010, the pair launched Snapdeal as a platform for daily deals, but in 2011, they extended it to become a full-fledged e-commerce business. Snapdeal quickly rose to prominence as one of India’s top online marketplaces. The success of the platform makes him one of the most famous business personalities in India.

4. Radhakishan Damani

Radhakishan Damani, a successful Indian billionaire best known for founding DMart, was born into a lower-middle-class Marwari family in Mumbai. When his father passed away, Damani’s ball-bearing business was forced to close. Damani started working at Dalal Street after his death. During this time, Damani amassed a sizeable chunk of money before leaving the stock exchange in 2000. In 2002, he built the first DMart in Powai; by 2010, the chain had 25 locations. There are already more than 230 DMart locations, and Radhakishan Damani ranked fourth in terms of wealth in India in 2020.

5. Mukesh Jagtiani

Mukesh Jagtiani, also referred to as “Micky” Jagtiani, is a businessman from India with Sindhi ancestry who resides in the UAE. In Kuwait, Jagtiani was born. Jagtiani established the Landmark Group in Dubai, which subsequently branched out into a number of specialised markets like fashion, electronics, furniture, and hotels. Over 45000 people are employed by The Landmark Group throughout the Persian Gulf, Middle East, and India. As of May 2021, Jagtiani, who entered Forbes’ list of billionaires in 2008, had a net worth of $3 billion. He is definitely one of the most famous business personalities in India. 

6. Dilip Shangvi

Dilip Shanghvi, who was raised primarily in Calcutta and has a bachelor’s in commerce from the University of Calcutta, was born in the Gujarati village of Amreli. Shanghvi started his career in Kolkata, where his father had a wholesale generic pharmaceuticals company. He began to consider creating his own pharmaceuticals during this time, and in 1982, with just Rs 10,000, he started the Sun Pharmaceutical Industries.  Sun purchased Ranbaxy in 2014, making it India’s biggest pharmaceutical firm. In October 2021, Shanghvi, who had a net worth of approximately $14 billion, was the 14th richest individual in India.

7. Ghanshyam Das Birla

G. D. Birla, who was born into the already wealthy Merchant family of the Birlas, rose to prominence as one of the family’s most significant members and eventually founded a number of significant businesses and institutions that still stand as a testament to his legacy. Birla had the idea to start a commercial bank using Indian capital after the Quit India Movement in 1942, and as a result, United Commercial Bank, subsequently known as UCO Bank, was created. In addition, Birla established BITS in Pilani, his hometown, which is today one of India’s most prestigious educational institutions.

8. Lakshmi Mittal

Mohanlal Mittal, the father of Lakshmi Mittal, was a Marwadi who ran the steel company Nippon Denro Ispat. As part of his father’s Ispat Industries, Lakshmi Mittal constructed his first steel facility in Indonesia in 1978 under the name Ispat International due to the restriction on steel production in India. In 1989, Mittal purchased a state-owned steel mill in Trinidad and Tobago. Over the subsequent 20 years, he made numerous other acquisitions, the largest of which being his 2006 purchase of Arcelor, which he renamed ArcelorMittal.

9. Ritesh Agrawal

Ritesh Agarwal was raised in Odisha and was born into a low-income household. Despite dropping out of college, Ritesh was chosen for the 2013 Thiel Fellowship. As the recipient of the Thiel Fellowship Program’s $100,000 grant, he founded a website for finding cheap lodging, which he introduced as OYO Rooms in 2013. Agarwal tripled his interest in OYO by purchasing shares worth $2 billion in 2019, which he did in September 2018 after raising $1 billion in cash. Ritesh Agarwal is currently the second-youngest self-made billionaire.

10. Azim Premji

Azim Premji is an Indian businessman and philanthropist who was born into a prominent Gujarati Muslim business family. He took over WIPRO after graduating from Stanford University with an engineering degree. The business was originally in the hydrogenated oil business, but Azim Premji expanded it into other industries such as soaps & toiletries, lighting, hydraulic cylinders, etc. Premji rebranded the company and moved it into the IT industry by producing microcomputers in order to capitalise on India’s IT growth. Over the past 20 years, he has devoted all of his time to advancing India’s educational system while also working on his business.

11. Shiv Nadar

Shiv Nadar is an Indian millionaire businessman who was raised in the town of Moolaipozhi in Madras Presidency (current-day Tamil Nadu). Beginning his career with Cooper Engineering Ltd. of the Walchand Group, he quickly quit to launch his own business. He finally established Microcomp in 1976 to sell tele-digital calculators in India and HCL. The business expanded internationally in 1980 when Far East Computers was established in Singapore. He gave his daughter Roshni Nadar control of the business in 2020, making her the country’s first female chairman of a publicly traded IT company.

12. Falguni Nayar

Falguni Nayar, a Mumbai native, completed her undergraduate studies at Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics before obtaining her master’s degree from IIM Ahmedabad. In 1985, she started her career as a consultant by working as a consultant for A F Ferguson & Co., a management consulting firm. She began working at Kotak Mahindra Group in 1993 and worked there for 19 years, holding the position of managing director from 2005 until her departure from the organisation in 2012. Falguni Nayar created Nykaa in the same year, when she was 50 years old. As of 2021, Nykaa was valued at $2.3 billion, boosting Nayar’s net worth to just under $1.1 billion.

13. Sachin Bansal

Sachin Bansal, a Chandigarh native who attended IIT Delhi after graduating, first worked for Amazon before launching his own e-commerce site. He founded Flipkart as an online book retailer as well, similar to Amazon. At first, Binny Bansal and Sachin Bansal ran their start-up out of a flat in Bangalore. In 2018, Bansal made his exit by selling his shares to Walmart. After leaving Flipkart, Bansal made a number of investments, including an investment of $100 million in Ola Cabs. Together with Ankit Agrawal, he established the financial services business Navi in 2018.

14. Deepinder Goyal

Deepinder Goyal, an Indian businessman who was born in Chandigarh, founded the well-known online meal delivery service Zomato. Goyal earned a BTech degree from IIT Delhi and had a brief career with Bain & Company. Goyal founded Foodiebay, later rebranded to Zomato, since he had always been interested in starting a food and services company. Zomato has received a lot of backing from investors and customers over the years, and in 2020 it will be recognised as a unicorn company. Goyal’s net worth was $650 million as of 2021.

15. N R Narayanamurthy

N R Narayanamurthy grew up in a middle-class Kannadiga family in Sidlaghatta, the capital city of the Kingdom of Mysore. He began working there as a research associate before rising to the position of Chief Systems Programmer. He worked on India’s first time-sharing computer system during this time. His startup business, Softronics, was a failure. Nevertheless, he invested Rs 10,000 to create Infosys in 1981, and he held the position of CEO for 21 years.

Top 15 Business Women

  1. Suman Agarwal – Co-founder & Director of Image Consulting Business Institute
  2. Falguni Nayar – Founder and CEO of Nykaa
  3. Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw – Chairperson and Managing Director of Biocon Ltd.
  4. Indra Nooyi – Former CEO of PepsiCo, Board of Directors – Amazon and Others
  5. Richa Kar – Founder and CEO of Zivame
  6. Sudha Murty – Teacher, Chairperson of The Infosys Foundation
  7. Priyanka Chopra – Actress, Film Producer, Restaurant and Haircare Brand Owner
  8. Faye D'Souza – Independent Indian Journalist
  9. Shradha Sharma – Founder of YourStory Media Pvt. Ltd.
  10. Vandana Luthra – Founder of VLCC
  11. Ritu Kumar – Fashion Designer
  12. Yasmin Karachiwala – Fitness Trainer, Owner of The Body Image Studio
  13. Nita Ambani – Reliance Foundation | Social Entrepreneur
  14. Vani Kola – Founder and Managing Director of Kalaari Capital
  15. Mehak Sagar – Co-founder of WedMeGood

title: Current Affairs 2023 International!
body_html:
Several devastating earthquakes, two ongoing wars that heightened geopolitical tensions, numerous instances of gun violence in the United States and the imprisonment of a popular ex-Prime Minister in Pakistan — 2023 was an eventful year which saw natural disasters and man-made conflicts test nations and citizens globally.

Here is a look at some of the key stories that took place around the world this year:

Earthquake in Turkey and Syria

Over 67,000 people were killed after a series of devastating tremors hit parts of Turkey and neighbouring Syria early on February 6. Thousands of buildings tumbled down, trapping tens of thousands of residents. Most of the damage was done by the 7.8 and 7.7 magnitude quakes that struck Antakya within hours. It is estimated to be the largest earthquake in Turkey since 1939. An estimated 59,000 people in southern and central Turkey were killed while over 8,000 citizens in war-torn Syria perished. The historic cities of Sanliurfa and Aleppo were among those affected.

India takes #1 spot

India’s estimated population overtook that of China, becoming the world’s most populous country early this year. The UNFPA’s State of World Population Report 2023 confirmed that India’s estimated population was 142.86 crore, marginally ahead of China at 142.57 crore. India’s population is also largely young, with 68 per cent being between the ages of 15 and 64 years, which is considered the working population of a country. About 25 per cent is between 0-14 years; 18 per cent between 10 and 19 years, 26 per cent between 10 and 24 years, and 7 per cent above 65 years.)

The lost submersible

The Titan submersible carrying five people onboard imploded in the North Atlantic Ocean on June 18. The submersible was part of a deep sea extreme tourism mission to visit the 111-year-old wreckage of the Titanic more than 12,000 feet underwater. After days of gruelling search and rescue mission, officials confirmed that a debris field was found around 500m away from the bow of the Titanic that was consistent with that of the 22-foot submersible.

Passengers onboard were Stockton Rush, the CEO of OceanGate, the company that ran and designed the expedition, Paul-Henri Nargeolet, a French deep-sea explorer and Titanic expert, Hamish Harding, a British businessman, Shahzada Dawood, a Pakistani-British businessman, and his son Suleman.

Russia-Ukraine war spills into second year

More than a year after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, the war continued with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy scrambling to mobilise a continuous supply of soldiers and weapons as key allies, Europe and America, slowed down the funding due to changes in internal politics. Though there is no concrete information on the number of casualties, UN estimates say that more than 10,000 Ukrainian civilians have been killed. A New York Times report said that over 5 lakh Ukrainian and Russian soldiers have been killed so far. Russian President Vladimir Putin, meanwhile, has maintained that the war will go on unless Kyiv does a deal that takes Moscow’s security concerns into account. “Either we get an agreement, agree on certain parameters (on the size and strength of Ukraine’s military)… or we solve this by force. This is what we will strive for,” he said.

Imran Khan’s arrest and Nawaz Sharif’s return

2022-2023 was an eventful year for Imran Khan. The cricketer-turned-politician, who was removed from Pakistan’s PM post via a no-confidence motion in April 2022, was arrested and jailed in the Toshakhana case, in which he is accused of not disclosing details of expensive gifts received while in office. Khan’s arrest was followed by days of drama in which his supporters clashed with law enforcement, including storming the army headquarters in Rawalpindi and the Corps Commander’s residence in Lahore. Meanwhile, the events also cleared the way for the return of former PM Nawaz Sharif, who was under exile in London for four years. His return just as the general elections are scheduled to take place early next year, is widely seen as a precursor for another stab at power.

The ongoing Israel-Hamas war

The ongoing Israel-Hamas war in Gaza has killed nearly 20,000 Palestinians, wounded tens of thousands more, and displaced 90% of the 2.3 million residents of the besieged enclave. The current conflict was triggered by the surprise Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, in which 1,200 Israelis were gunned down in their homes, at a music festival and other public places by militants who overcame the country’s famed security and intelligence measures. The attack left thousands wounded and over 240 others were taken hostage, of which about half have been released as a part of a temporary ceasefire earlier this month. Meanwhile, in a bid to stop the war, the United Nations had taken a series of extraordinary measures, including the triggering of Article 99 of the UN Charter. A December 13 UNGA vote demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in the conflict was adopted with an overwhelming majority of 153 nations (including India) voting in its favour, 10 voting against (including US and Israel) and 23 abstentions, but it has not translated to action on the ground.

Bangladesh elections and protests

As Bangladesh gears up for elections on January 7, the country has been rocked by violence in the lead-up to it as supporters of the main opposition BNP and the ruling Awami League clashed on numerous instances. The BNP has been demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been ruling the nation for a combined period of nearly 19 years. The BNP has demanded that Hasina resign to facilitate free and fair elections under a non-party interim government, under which four elections from 1991 to 2008 were held. As The Indian Express had reported,  the December 2008 elections installed Hasina’s Awami League, while the subsequent 2014 and 2008 polls were held under the incumbent government, which scrapped the constitutional provision after assuming office in January 2009.

A blip in Canada-India relations

The India-Canada diplomatic relationship turned frosty this year after Canadian PM Justin Trudeau claimed that there was a “potential link” between the Indian government and the killing of a pro-Khalistan leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada earlier this year. Nijjar, who was the head of the Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara Sahib in Surrey and the chief of the separatist organisation Khalistan Tiger Force (KTF), was shot by two unidentified men outside the gurdwara in June. Trudeau’s accusations, which India has denied as “absurd and motivated” has set off a chain of reactions, including the expulsion of several Canadian diplomats from India and the temporary suspension of visa services in Canada. Months later, the United States Department of Justice (DoJ) charged an Indian national, Nikhil Gupta, for his involvement in a plot to murder a US-based Khalistani leader.

2023 Nashville school shooting

School shootings have, unfortunately, become a familiar part of the news cycle in the US. In March 2023, a mass shooting at an elementary school in Nashville, Tennessee grabbed headlines after a former student opened fire in The Covenant School building, killing six people, including three nine‑year‑old children. The shooter was shot dead by the police.  A still image from surveillance video shows what the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department describe as mass shooting suspect Audrey Elizabeth Hale (left) walking in The Covenant School carrying weapons in Nashville, Tennessee, US, March 27, 2023. (Metropolitan Nashville Police Department/Handout via Reuters)

Authorities said that Audrey Hale had drawn a detailed map of the school, including potential entry points, and conducted surveillance of the building before carrying out the massacre at the Christian school.

The Nepal quake

More than 150 people were killed and hundreds of others injured after a 6.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Nepal on November 3. The quake, whose epicentre was at Ramidanda, about 550 km from the capital city of Kathmandu, was the country’s deadliest since 2015.https://www.youtube.com/embed/_4fyBOUfSgA?version=3&rel=1&showsearch=0&showinfo=1&iv_load_policy=1&fs=1&hl=en-US&autohide=2&wmode=transparent

The high death toll was partially due to the timing of the tremors, which hit the country at 11.47 pm (local time). “If it had happened during the day, some people would have been out for work, some would have been in open areas, but because it happened late at night, the damage is more,” a local activist told The Indian Express.

title: Current Affairs 2023 India!
body_html:
Lunar crown:
Chandrayaan-3 successfully lands at lunar south pole. In a giant leap for its space programme, India's Moon mission Chandrayaan-3 touched down on the lunar south pole on Wednesday, propelling the country to an exclusive club of four and making it the first country to land on the uncharted surface.

India gets a new Parliament
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on May 28 inaugurated the new Parliament building and installed the sacred 'Sengol' in the Lok Sabha chamber. The new building has 888 seats in the Lok Sabha chamber and 384 seats in the Rajya Sabha chamber.

Supreme court upholds Article 370 abrogation

In a historic decision on December 11, the Supreme Court delivered its long-awaited verdict on the contentious issue of Article 370. The Supreme Court upheld the government's decision to repeal Article 370, which granted special status to the former state of Jammu and Kashmir and said steps should be taken to hold elections in the assembly by September 30 of next year.

Sinking serenity: Land subsidence in Joshimath
Joshimath, the gateway to famous pilgrimage sites like Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib and international skiing destination Auli, faced a major challenge due to land subsidence. It sank gradually with huge cracks developing in houses, roads and fields there, with over 65% of houses in town suffering due to the subsidence.

Rails of tragedy: Balasore triple train collission claims more than 280 lives
The Shalimar-Chennai Central Coromandel Express, Bengaluru-Howrah Super Fast Express and a goods train were involved in the pile-up, which was described as one of India's worst train accidents. More than 280 people lost their lives and five others succumbed to their injuries in hospitals, while 1,208 were injured.

Beyond the mat: Wrestlers hold protest against WFI chief Brij Bhushan Singh
On January 18, wrestlers initiated a protest at Jantar Mantar, alleging sexual exploitation and intimidation by WFI chief Brij Bhushan Singh Sharan, demanding his resignation and the federation's dissolution. On May 28, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia, among others, faced charges for rioting and obstructing public servants during a march toward the newly inaugurated Parliament by PM Narendra Modi.

Heartbreak for team India; Australia create another record
Australia clinched their sixth ICC Cricket World Cup title, defeating India by 6 wickets. Travis Head's stellar 137-run innings led the way, earning applause from his teammates for his outstanding performance on the grand stage. This was the only defeat team India suffered in the entire competition, which was held on its soil.

Same-sex marriage remains a call for future

The Supreme Court on October 17 refused to grant legal recognition to same-sex marriage under the Special Marriage Act, saying that it is within Parliament's ambit to change the law. A five-judge constitution bench headed by Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud said as he began his verdict in the matter that "courts cannot make law but can interpret and give effect to it."

India in space: Isro successfully launches its solar mission
On September 2 Isro's Aditya-L1 mission was launched. It is India's first mission dedicated to studying the Sun, specifically the photosphere, chromosphere, and corona of Sun. It has 7 distinct payloads developed, all developed indigenously. Five by Isro and two by academic institutes in collaboration with the space agency. 


​Silkyara miracle: Workers successfully rescued after 17 days
On November 12, 2023, a portion of the under-construction Silkyara Bend–Barkot tunnel, intended to link National Highway 134 in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand, collapsed. Forty-one workers were trapped for 17 days and were successfully rescued from the tunnel on November 28. 

Breaking barriers: Parliament passes Women's reservation bill

"A defining moment in our nation's democratic journey," Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on September 22 as Rajya Sabha passed the historic women's reservation bill with 214 MPs voting in favour and none against. The 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' became the first bill to be passed by Parliament after it shifted to the new building on Tuesday.

An unwanted record: A record 143 MPs suspended

A total of 143 MPs - 97 from Lok Sabha and 46 from Rajya Sabha - were suspended for creating a ruckus and disrupting proceedings in both Houses, while they were demanding a statement from Union Minister Amit Shah about the Parliament security breach incident.

7 Sisters

The insurgency in Nagaland, in northeastern India, is an ongoing conflict fought between the ethnic Nagas and the governments of India. Nagaland inhabited by the Nagas is located at the tri-junction border of India on the West and South, north and Myanmar on the East. 2,000 Killed total (official).

Preface:

International Management Institute (IMI) is India’s first corporate sponsored Business School founded in 1981 with the original campus in New Delhi. Corporate sponsors include RPG Enterprises (lead sponsor), ITC, Nestle, Tata Chemicals, British Oxygen, SAIL, and Williamson Magor. Over the last four decades, IMI has emerged as one of the best Business Schools in the country, upholding its reputation for developing business leaders and providing high-quality management education. IMI New Delhi has global linkages with leading schools in Europe, North America, and Asia. The institute is accredited by AMBA, SAQS, AACSB, NBA, and approved by AICTE. Located in the heart of the city, IMI has easy access to major corporate houses. The institute boasts intellectual capital from distinguished and renowned professors. IMI has a vast alumni network, with 7000+ members holding notable positions globally in companies such as Morgan Stanley, Google, Bain & Co, Microsoft, Boston Consulting Group, McKinsey & Co, Airbus, CBRE, etc. IMI offers excellent summer internship and final placement opportunities across various domains.

Group Activity Exercises for GDPI Cetking Number 6 - Mayday Mayday

Mayday-Mayhem-Group-Activity-from-CetkingDownload


Case for group Activity Exercises for GDPI . Download full group activity with solution

You and your companions have just survived the crash of a small plane.  Both the pilot and co-pilot were killed in the crash.  It is mid-January , and you are in Northern Kashmir.  The daily temperature is 25 below zero, and the night time temperature is 40 below zero.  There is snow on the ground, and the countryside is wooded with several creeks criss-crossing the area.  The nearest town is 20 miles away.  You are all dressed in city clothes appropriate for a business meeting.  Your group of survivors managed to salvage the following items:

  1. A ball of steel wool
  2. A small axe
  3. A loaded  .45-caliber pistol
  4. Can of butter
  5. Newspapers (one per person)
  6. Cigarette lighter (without fluid)
  7. Extra shirt and pants for each survivor
  8. 20 x 20 ft. piece of heavy-duty canvas
  9. A sectional air map made of plastic
  10. One quart of 100-proof whiskey
  11. A compass
  12. Family-size chocolate bars (one per person)

Stage 1

Your task as a group is to list the above 12 items in order of importance for your survival.  List the uses for each (not asked in the Group Activity but for your purpose/practice)

Stage 2 Group Ranking

Now start the group discussion and try to agree to a final list of ranking before the time is up.

body_html:
Good Introductions Sample for interviews

title: Top 10 Internship Ideas & Sample Certificate
body_html:
Why Every MBA Aspirant Should Do a Project with Their Family Business or Employer

One of the most underrated yet powerful ways to gain early business exposure is right within your reach — your own family. Whether your family runs a business, works in a corporate job, or is associated with any professional sector, there lies an incredible opportunity for MBA aspirants to get a real-world understanding of how organizations function.

A mini-project or internship under a family member's company or professional domain doesn’t require formal HR approval or official internship letters. An email from your parent, uncle, aunt, or any close relative who is employed in an organization or runs a business is enough to validate the experience for B-school applications or your CV.

The best part? You don’t need to physically visit the office every day. The aim is to research, interact, and observe business operations, supply chains, sales strategies, marketing efforts, financial flows, or people management — depending on the role your family member is involved in.

If your family runs a business — you’ve struck gold. You can go deeper, take on a live problem, suggest improvements, or even test out a small marketing or digital experiment. For those in service roles, you can observe the functioning of that department — from logistics and IT to finance and customer support — and document learnings.

The core idea is to turn everyday access into strategic exposure. B-schools love candidates who show initiative, curiosity, and the ability to learn from their environment. A family-led project signals all three.

ROADMAP: How to Structure Your Family Project Internship

STEP 1: Identify Opportunity

  • Ask your parents, siblings, uncles, aunts what they do.
  • Find who works in a field related to business, operations, sales, etc.

STEP 2: Define the Scope

  • Choose a topic: e.g. marketing, HR processes, vendor management.
  • Draft 2-3 goals for your internship (ex: "Understand vendor selection process").

STEP 3: Get Email Confirmation

  • Ask for a simple email from your family member confirming you're helping as a learning project.

STEP 4: Research & Document

  • Talk to 2-3 people in the team (remotely).
  • Research competitors or similar companies online.
  • Write a report/presentation on your findings.

Sample Internship Ideas Based on Family Background

Creating meaningful and impactful projects for interns is essential to provide them with valuable experience and contribute to the organization's goals. Here are ten top project ideas for interns in an office setting:

  • Market Research Analysis: Interns can conduct market research to gather insights about competitors, customer preferences, and industry trends. They can analyze the data and present their findings to help the company make informed decisions.
  • Social Media Campaign: Interns can develop and execute a social media campaign to increase the company's online presence and engagement. This could include creating content calendars, designing posts, and analyzing campaign performance.
  • Process Improvement: Interns can analyze existing workflows and processes within the organization to identify inefficiencies. They can suggest improvements and create a plan to implement these changes, enhancing overall productivity.
  • Customer Feedback Survey: Interns can design and conduct surveys to gather feedback from customers about the company's products or services. They can analyze the results and provide recommendations for improvements based on the feedback.
  • Content Creation: Interns can create content for the company's blog, website, or marketing materials. This could include writing articles, designing infographics, or producing videos to engage the target audience.
  • Data Analysis Project: Interns can work with data from various departments to identify trends, patterns, and insights. They can use tools like Excel, SQL, or data visualization software to present their findings and support decision-making processes.
  • Event Planning: Interns can assist in planning and organizing company events, such as workshops, webinars, or team-building activities. They can handle logistics, coordinate with vendors, and ensure the event runs smoothly.
  • Sales Support: Interns can support the sales team by researching potential leads, creating sales materials, and assisting with CRM management. They can help streamline the sales process and contribute to achieving sales targets.
  • HR Initiatives: Interns can work on HR projects such as employee engagement surveys, onboarding programs, or diversity and inclusion initiatives. They can help improve the overall employee experience and company culture.
  • Website Optimization: Interns can analyze the company's website for usability and performance issues. They can suggest and implement improvements to enhance user experience, SEO, and overall site functionality.

These projects not only provide interns with valuable experience and skill development but also offer tangible benefits to the organization.

Internship Certificate Sample

Certificate of Completion of Internship

This is to certify that [Intern’s Name] has successfully completed a Summer Internship program as [Intern’s Title/Position] at [Organisation Name], located at [Organisation Address].The internship program ran from [Start Date] to [End Date].

Throughout the internship, [Intern’s Name] demonstrated a strong work ethic and made valuable contributions to the team.[He/She/] actively participated in [List of Projects], where [He/She/] played a key role in [Specific accomplishments or contributions]. [Intern’s Name] also developed their skills in [List of skills learned], which will be beneficial in their future endeavours.

We are pleased to award [Intern’s Name] this certificate in recognition of their successful completion of the internship program.

[Signature]

[Name of Supervisor/Manager]

[Title]

[Contact Information (Optional)]

[Official Seal]

title: Power Verbs for Spoken English Part 1
body_html:
Enriching your spoken English with powerful verbs can make your communication more vivid and precise. Here are 20 powerful verbs along with their meanings:

  1. Articulate: To express an idea clearly and effectively.
  2. Amplify: To make something louder or more powerful; to increase.
  3. Assert: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.
  4. Bolster: To support or strengthen.
  5. Clarify: To make something clear or easier to understand.
  6. Convey: To communicate or make known.
  7. Demonstrate: To show clearly and deliberately.
  8. Elicit: To draw out a response or reaction.
  9. Emphasize: To give special importance or prominence to something.
  10. Engage: To attract and hold someone's interest or attention.
  11. Facilitate: To make an action or process easier.
  12. Illuminate: To make something clear or easier to understand by explaining.
  13. Instigate: To initiate or bring about an action or event.
  14. Mitigate: To make something less severe, serious, or painful.
  15. Negotiate: To discuss something in order to reach an agreement.
  16. Persuade: To convince someone to do or believe something through reasoning or argument.
  17. Reinforce: To strengthen or support, especially with additional personnel or material.
  18. Resolve: To settle or find a solution to a problem or contentious matter.
  19. Scrutinize: To examine or inspect closely and thoroughly.
  20. Transform: To make a thorough or dramatic change in form, appearance, or character.

Using these verbs in your speech can help convey your thoughts more powerfully and leave a lasting impression on your listeners.

Why Power Vocab is needed?

A powerful vocabulary is essential for improving spoken English because it enhances clarity and precision, allowing you to express your thoughts more accurately and effectively. This precision reduces misunderstandings and makes your speech more engaging and interesting, capturing and maintaining the listener's attention. Moreover, a strong vocabulary bolsters your ability to persuade others, presenting your ideas compellingly and articulating your arguments convincingly. It also boosts your confidence, as you're less likely to struggle for the right word, leading to more fluent and natural speech. In professional settings, a robust vocabulary demonstrates intelligence, competence, and a strong command of the language, which is crucial for career advancement. Additionally, it enhances expressiveness, enabling you to convey emotions, describe situations vividly, and add nuance to your speech. A wide vocabulary improves your comprehension of complex texts and conversations, thus enhancing your overall communication skills. It also allows you to adapt your language to different contexts and audiences, whether in formal meetings or casual conversations. Learning new words often involves understanding new concepts and cultural nuances, broadening your perspective and intercultural communication skills. Ultimately, using a powerful vocabulary leaves a strong impression on others, showing that you are articulate and knowledgeable, which is particularly beneficial in social and professional interactions. Investing in expanding your vocabulary is a crucial step towards mastering spoken English and becoming a more effective and confident communicator.

title: Absconding or Laid Off Work Experience is Valid?
body_html:
Background Check

Most MBA Colleges wont do it but Once you get placed, Most organizations conduct a "background check" as part of their hiring process. You aren't required to mention your previous experience upfront, as the norms dictate that you submit the relevant documents. If you happened to leave a job abruptly and provide a weak excuse for not submitting the necessary documents immediately, be aware that your employee ID links all your information to the verifying party. Consequently, the HR team will have full access to details about your departure and your rehire eligibility.

How Employee Verification is done
Understanding the scope of background verification involves knowing the types of checks typically conducted during the hiring process. These checks can vary based on factors such as the industry of the business, the specific position being filled, and the level of scrutiny permitted by law. However, most organizations, regardless of industry, commonly perform identity checks, which form the basis for other verifications, along with educational verification, employment history, professional qualifications, and reference checks.

title: Valid Proofs for Achievements
body_html:
Showcasing achievements effectively requires credible and verifiable evidence. Whether for job applications, academic pursuits, or professional recognition, having valid proof of your accomplishments is essential. Here are three key forms of documentation that can substantiate your achievements:

Certificates of Wins and Event Participation

Certificates serve as formal recognition of your accomplishments and are one of the most widely accepted proofs. These can include awards for winning competitions, certificates for participation in events, or accolades for organizing initiatives. Ensure that the certificate includes your name, the event name, the awarding body, and the date of the achievement. Digital copies of certificates are equally valid and can be easily shared during applications or reviews. Certificates provide a tangible and official record of your achievements, adding credibility to your claims.

Official Email Communication of Accolades

Email communication from authoritative figures, such as supervisors, event organizers, or academic heads, is another strong proof of achievement. An email congratulating you on your performance, recognizing your efforts in an event, or confirming your role in an accomplishment holds significant value. These emails serve as dated, verifiable records and can often include details not covered in certificates, such as qualitative feedback or specific contributions. Retaining these communications as part of your portfolio demonstrates professionalism and attention to detail.

Photos of Achievements

Photos provide visual evidence of your participation or success in events. These could include images of you receiving awards, delivering presentations, or leading a team activity. Ensure the photos clearly show the context of the achievement, such as banners, certificates, or the event setting. Including captions or additional details when presenting these photos makes them more impactful. Visual documentation not only reinforces your claims but also adds a personal touch to your profile, making it more relatable and engaging.

In conclusion, certificates, official email communications, and photos collectively provide a comprehensive and credible set of proofs for achievements. Using these effectively can help you stand out and substantiate your accomplishments with confidence.

title: Is it Okay to Get Salary in Cash?
body_html:
Proving your work-ex in the IIMs you will require following documents:

  1. Joining letter (not the Appointment Letter)
  2. Work-experience certificate issued by your company
  3. First month and last three months payslips (cash salary candidates also should provide salary slips)

In India, receiving a salary in cash is a common practice, especially in smaller businesses or informal sectors. While it is perfectly legal, it comes with certain responsibilities and considerations to ensure compliance with the law and financial security. Here are three key aspects to consider when being paid in cash:

Legality

Receiving your salary in cash is legally permissible in India. However, you must comply with applicable tax laws. If your annual income exceeds the basic exemption limit of ₹2.5 lakh, you are required to declare this income and pay taxes as per the Income Tax Act. Employers, even when paying in cash, are obliged to deduct TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) if your income falls within the taxable bracket. Failing to report such income can lead to penalties and scrutiny from tax authorities, making it essential to ensure your cash salary is accounted for and tax-compliant.

Documentation

One of the challenges of receiving a salary in cash is the lack of automatic transaction records that a bank payment provides. To address this, it is crucial to maintain proper documentation. Request a salary slip, signed receipt, or any written confirmation from your employer as proof of payment. These records are not only necessary for filing your income tax return (ITR) but also for other purposes such as applying for loans, credit cards, or visas. Proper documentation safeguards you from potential financial or legal issues arising from undocumented income.

Tax Compliance

Declaring your income in your ITR is non-negotiable, regardless of whether your salary is received in cash or credited to your bank account. Failing to report cash income can lead to legal complications and hefty fines. By accurately declaring your cash salary, you maintain compliance with the law and establish a verifiable financial history. This transparency is vital for building financial credibility and avoiding unnecessary stress during tax assessments or audits.

In conclusion, while receiving a salary in cash is acceptable and often practical for small businesses, it requires a proactive approach to ensure proper documentation and tax compliance. By adhering to these practices, you can enjoy the flexibility of cash payments without facing any legal or financial hurdles.

title: 6 Killer Sample Salary Slips

  1. Joining letter (not the Appointment Letter)
  2. Work-experience certificate issued by your company
  3. First month and last three months payslips (cash salary candidates also should provide salary slips)

If you have prior work experience or have worked in a family business, you can create your own salary slip to showcase your employment history for official purposes. A self-created salary slip should include your name, designation, duration of employment, earnings, and deductions. Ensure it is signed and stamped by an authorized person (such as a family business head or supervisor) to validate authenticity. This approach is acceptable when applying for loans, visas, or academic programs, as long as the details are accurate and the business is legitimate. Proper documentation adds credibility and supports your professional profile.
